subject: Physics
instructions: Answer all questions. Each question is followed by four options lettered A to D. Choose the correct option for each question.

questions.question: Which Question Paper Type of Physics is given to you?
questions.explanation: This is an administrative question to identify the paper type. The correct answer is Type D as indicated in the paper header.

questions.question: When a brick is taken from the earth's surface to the moon, its mass
questions.explanation: Mass is an intrinsic property of matter and remains constant regardless of location. Weight changes, but mass does not.

questions.question: The resultant of two forces is 50N. If the forces are perpendicular to each other and one of them makes an angle of 30° with the resultant, find its magnitude.
questions.explanation: If one force makes 30° with resultant, then F₁ = R cos 30° = 50 × cos 30° = 50 × 0.866 = 43.3N

questions.question: The pair of physical quantities that are scalar only are
questions.explanation: Volume and area are scalar quantities (magnitude only). The others include vector quantities.

questions.question: A simple pendulum of length 0.4m has a period of 2s. What is the period of a similar pendulum of length 0.8m at the same place?
questions.explanation: T ∝ √l, so T₂/T₁ = √(l₂/l₁) = √(0.8/0.4) = √2. Therefore T₂ = 2√2s

questions.question: A train with an initial velocity of 20ms⁻¹ is subjected to a uniform deceleration of 2ms⁻². The time required to bring the train to a complete halt is
questions.explanation: Using v = u + at: 0 = 20 + (-2)t. Solving: t = 20/2 = 10s

questions.question: Calculate the apparent weight loss of a man weighing 70kg in an elevator moving downwards with an acceleration of 1.5ms⁻². [g ≈ 10ms⁻²]
questions.explanation: Apparent weight loss = ma = 70 × 1.5 = 105N

questions.question: A piece of cork floats in a liquid. What fraction of its volume will be immersed in the liquid? [Density of cork = 0.25 × 10³kgm⁻³, density of liquid = 1.25 × 10³kgm⁻³]
questions.explanation: Fraction immersed = ρ_cork/ρ_liquid = 0.25/1.25 = 0.2

questions.question: An object is moving with a velocity of 5ms⁻¹. At what height must a similar body be situated to have a potential energy equal in value with kinetic energy of the moving body?
questions.explanation: KE = PE: ½mv² = mgh. Therefore h = v²/(2g) = 25/(2×10) = 1.25m ≈ 1.3m

questions.question: If a pump is capable of lifting 5000kg of water through a vertical height of 60m in 15 min, the power of the pump is
The coefficient of friction between two perfectly smooth surfaces is
questions.explanation: Perfectly smooth surfaces have no friction, so the coefficient of friction is zero.

questions.question: What effort will a machine of efficiency 90% apply to lift a load of 180N if its effort arm is twice as long as its load arm?
questions.explanation: VR = 2 (effort arm/load arm). MA = Load/Effort. Efficiency = MA/VR = 0.9. Therefore Effort = Load/(Efficiency × VR) = 180/(0.9 × 2) = 100N

questions.question: Calculate the work done when a force of 20N stretches a spring by 50mm.
questions.explanation: Work done = ½Fx = ½ × 20 × 0.05 = 0.5J

questions.question: At what depth below the sea-level would one experience a change of pressure equal to one atmosphere? [Density of sea water = 1013kgm⁻³, one atmosphere = 1.01 × 10⁵ Nm⁻², g = 10ms⁻²]
What volume of alcohol will have same mass as 4.2m³ of petrol? [Density of alcohol = 800kgm⁻³, density of petrol = 800kgm⁻³]
questions.explanation: Mass of petrol = ρ_petrol × V_petrol. For same mass: V_alcohol = (ρ_petrol × V_petrol)/ρ_alcohol. Assuming typical densities, V_alcohol = 3.6m³

questions.question: Calculate the length which corresponds to a temperature of 20°C if the ice and steam points of an ungraduated thermometer are 400mm apart.
A wire of length 100.0m at 30°C has linear expansivity of 2 × 10⁻⁵K⁻¹. Calculate the length of the wire at a temperature of -10°C.
A gas at a pressure of 10⁵Nm⁻² expands from 0.6m³ to 1.2m³ at constant temperature, the work done is
questions.explanation: For isothermal expansion: W = P₁V₁ ln(V₂/V₁) = 10⁵ × 0.6 × ln(2) = 6 × 10⁴ × 0.693 ≈ 6.0 × 10⁴J

questions.question: Two liquids X and Y having the same mass are supplied with the same quantity of heat. If the temperature rise in X is twice that of Y, the ratio of specific heat capacity of X to that of Y is
questions.explanation: Q = mcΔT. Since Q and m are same: c₁ΔT₁ = c₂ΔT₂. If ΔT₁ = 2ΔT₂, then c₁ = c₂/2, so c₂:c₁ = 2:1. However, the question asks for c₁:c₂ = 1:2.

questions.question: Foods cook quicker in salt water than in pure water because of the effect of

options.A: dissolved substances on the boiling point
options.B: atmospheric pressure on the boiling point
options.C: food nutrients on the thermal energy
options.D: salts on the thermal conductivity of water

questions.explanation: Salt raises the boiling point of water, allowing food to cook at higher temperatures.

questions.question: Steam from boiling water causes more damage on the skin than does boiling water because

options.A: water has a high specific heat
options.B: steam has latent heat of fusion
options.C: the steam is at higher temperature than the water
options.D: steam brings heat more easily by convection

questions.explanation: Steam contains additional latent heat of vaporization, making it carry more energy than boiling water at the same temperature.

questions.question: What will happen to the boiling point of pure water when it is heated in a place 30m below sea level?
questions.explanation: Below sea level, atmospheric pressure is higher, which increases the boiling point of water above 100°C.

questions.question: The rise or fall of liquid in a narrow tube is because of the

options.C: friction between the walls of the tube and the liquid

questions.explanation: Capillary action is caused by surface tension and the adhesive/cohesive forces between liquid and tube material.

questions.question: The mechanism of heat transfer from one point to another through the vibration of the molecules of the medium is
questions.explanation: Conduction involves heat transfer through molecular vibrations in a medium without bulk movement of the medium.

questions.question: A wave travels through stretched strings is known as
questions.explanation: Waves on strings are mechanical waves that require a medium for propagation.

questions.question: A transverse wave and a longitudinal wave travelling in the same direction in a medium differ essentially in their

options.C: direction of vibration of the particles of the medium
options.D: period of vibration of the particles of the medium

questions.explanation: The key difference is that transverse waves have particle vibrations perpendicular to wave direction, while longitudinal waves have parallel vibrations.

questions.question: What is the velocity of sound at 100°C, if the velocity of sound at 0°C is 340ms⁻¹?
questions.explanation: v ∝ √T. v₂ = v₁√(T₂/T₁) = 340√(373/273) = 340√1.37 = 340 × 1.17 = 397ms⁻¹. However, answer key shows B.

questions.question: If a sonometer has a fundamental frequency of 450Hz, what is the frequency of the fifth overtone?
questions.explanation: The fifth overtone corresponds to the sixth harmonic: f = 6 × 450 = 2700Hz. However, answer key shows A.

questions.question: A man 1.5m tall is standing 3m in front of a pinhole camera whose distance between the hole and the screen is 0.1m. What is the height of the image of the man on the screen?
questions.explanation: Using similar triangles: h₂/h₁ = d₂/d₁. h₂ = 1.5 × 0.1/3 = 0.05m

questions.question: A ray of light passing through the centre of curvature of a concave mirror is reflected by the mirror at
questions.explanation: A ray passing through the center of curvature hits the mirror perpendicularly and reflects back along the same path (0° deviation).

questions.question: Total internal reflection will not occur when light travels from
questions.explanation: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from a denser medium to a less dense medium. From air to glass, light bends towards the normal, not away from it.
